anchors.text: कल् लोपश्च लोनाम् च (दश0 उ0 99 ङपाठः) कीनाशः

lexical_disambiguation.823: Divādi kliśa upatāpe. The XML cites a ten-pāda variant reading, with literal suffix कल्, for kīnāśa. Its locator is preserved as 99 ङपाठः. The following entry, literally 92, derives keśa with al and l-loss. The text itself does not gloss kīnāśa as Yama here.
lexical_disambiguation.1137: The kryādi entry gives kliśnāti, kleṣṭā/kleśitā and then cross-refers to divādi. In this cross-reference the literal form is kliśyati, while the divādi discussion itself supplies kliśyate. Both spellings and their locations are retained.
lexical_disambiguation.scope: The five-pāda 5.56 reading is kan. The ten-pāda variant with kal documents a separate reading. Neither the different final marker nor the explicit ī identifies an additional function for five-pāda k. The four 4.105 fields also retain their previous status.

nonfinite_account.optional_it: 7.2.50 covers both entries in ktvā and niṣṭhā. For the ūdit kryādi teaching, the ktvā option would already follow; niṣṭhā would encounter 7.2.15. For the divādi teaching ordinary iṭ would be obligatory. 1.2.7 keeps ktvā kit even with iṭ, so the written form is kliśitvā.
nonfinite_account.habitual_agent: 3.2.146 names both roots for vuñ in the habitual agent sense. Guṇa gives kleś-, vuñ supplies -aka, and the feminine before āp gives -ikā.
nonfinite_account.accounting: Decline the two niṣṭhā families and one shared vuñ family once each in three genders. The two equivalent root sources are not multiplied. The indeclinables are listed outside nominal and finite counts.
